items.entity: square design domain - physical side length / units / thickness
items.description: Sec. 4.6 (Square Domain Study) only says 'a standard square design domain'. The 1:1 aspect ratio is clear, but no side length or units are given, and the Fig. 6 caption adds nothing. With square Q4 elements and a nodal load, compliance does not depend on side length; with a distributed load, the total force scales with it.
readings: L = 64 length units (unit element size, matching the 64x64 dataset grid)
a physical bracket size, e.g. L = 200 mm

items.entity: FE grid of the square domain
items.description: Sec. 4.6 never states the case-1 grid. The 64x64 resolution is implied only indirectly: Sec. 4.7.3 ('fixed 64x64 resolution of the TopoDiff dataset'), Table 8 ('64x64 domain') and Appendix C (k=64). The text does not say whether 64 counts elements or nodes/pixels, or what element type is used.
readings: 63x63 Q4 elements (64x64 nodes = image pixel grid)

items.entity: wall-side supports of the shelf bracket
items.description: Sec. 4.6 only says 'As shown in Fig. 6'; the text never says where the bracket is held. A wall-mounted bracket points to one vertical edge, but a fully restrained edge and discrete fastener points are both possible. If the case is a dataset sample, its supports are one of the 42 training / 5 test BC templates from Sec. 4.1, which the text never lists.
readings: whole left edge restrained (x = 0, 0 <= y <= L)
two fastener nodes only: top-left (0, L) and bottom-left (0, 0) corners
two short segments at the top and bottom of the left edge (y in [0, 0.1L] and [0.9L, L])
upper half of the left edge only (y in [0.5L, L])
any of the above on the right edge instead (mirrored layout)

items.entity: restrained DOFs at the bracket supports
items.description: The text never says which displacement components are restrained. Sec. 4.1 says only 'boundary conditions', and the Fig. 10 caption calls the markers just 'constrained boundary supports'.
readings: fully clamped: ux = uy = 0 at all support nodes
upper fastener pinned (ux = uy = 0), lower support restrains ux only (bearing against the wall)
ux restrained along the whole wall edge, uy restrained at a single node

items.description: The load location is conveyed only by Fig. 6. 'Shelf bracket' suggests the upper (shelf) edge, but not where along it; dataset loads sit at 'random unconstrained boundary nodes' (Sec. 4.1).
readings: top free corner (x = L, y = L, wall at x = 0)
top edge at mid-span (x = 0.5L, y = L)
free vertical edge at mid-height (x = L, y = 0.5L)

items.description: The text does not say whether the shelf load is a single nodal force, as in the single-load dataset (Sec. 4.1, Sec. 4.7.3), or is spread along the shelf edge, as a real shelf would load the bracket.
readings: uniformly distributed load over the entire top edge
uniform load over the outer half of the top edge (x in [0.5L, L])

items.description: The direction is not stated. Gravity suggests vertical, but dataset loads use angles in {0, pi/6, ..., pi} (Sec. 4.1), so an inclined load is possible. With a single load, reversing the sign does not change the layout.
readings: vertical (downward gravity; same layout as angle pi/2 in the dataset convention)
inclined at pi/3 or 2pi/3 from horizontal
inclined at pi/6 or 5pi/6 from horizontal

items.description: No force value is given, although Sec. 4.6 reports absolute compliances (5.0506 for the ground truth; 4.9962, 5.0398 and 5.0772 for the generated designs).
readings: a physical shelf load, e.g. |F| = 100 N (compliance scales with |F|^2)

items.entity: target volume fraction v_f of case 1
items.description: Sec. 4.6 gives no volume fraction for the shelf bracket (it may appear only in Fig. 6). The pretrained model covers 0.30 to 0.50 in 0.02 steps (Sec. 4.1).

No passive regions are mentioned. A practical shelf bracket might need a solid shelf seat, a wall plate or fastener holes, but the dataset format (Sec. 4.1: BCs, load and volume fraction only) suggests the whole square is designable.
readings: passive solid strip along the top (shelf) edge and/or the wall edge
passive void regions such as fastener holes

items.entity: Young's modulus E and out-of-plane thickness t
items.description: No Young's modulus or thickness is given anywhere; Sec. 3.1 defines K only symbolically.
Neither Poisson's ratio nor plane stress vs. plane strain is stated for the SIMP ground truth or the FEA evaluation (Sec. 4.1, 4.2).
The ground truth is 'obtained by SIMP' (Sec. 4.6; dataset in Sec. 4.1), but no penalization exponent is given.
Eq. (1) imposes 0 < x_min <= x <= 1 but gives no value for x_min. The same value sets the stiffness of void elements in the binarized compliance evaluation (Sec. 4.2).
The text never says whether the SIMP run that produced the ground truth used a sensitivity filter, a density filter, projection, or no filter.
No filter radius is stated. It controls minimum member size and therefore strut count, which is exactly what distinguishes the case-1 designs (one, two or three internal struts, Sec. 4.6).

items.entity: SIMP optimizer, initial design and stopping criterion
items.description: The text gives no update scheme, move limit, starting design or stopping rule. The 'Findings' paragraph of Sec. 4.6 attributes better-than-ground-truth designs to SIMP local optima, so these settings can change the reference layout.
readings: OC, move limit 0.2, uniform start x = v_f, stop when max density change < 0.01

items.description: Sec. 4.1 says each dataset sample stores the SIMP 'minimum compliance', while Sec. 4.2 evaluates compliance by FEA on designs binarized at tau = 0.5. It is unclear which definition gives the case-1 value 5.0506, and what stiffness void elements get in the binarized analysis.
readings: final SIMP objective on the penalized grey-scale design
FEA of the ground truth thresholded at 0.5, voids at x_min stiffness
FEA of the thresholded ground truth, voids at 1e-9*E0
